To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the AM symbiosis is a complex interaction between two different organisms, the fungus and the plant, which can be studied at different levels, from the whole plant, to the cellular and molecular levels.

the AM symbiosis alleviates the negative effects of water deficit on the host plants by: 1. improving plant water relations; 2. reducing oxidative stress; 3. increasing the plant ability to accumulate compatible solutes; 4. improving plant nutrient uptake; 5. reducing stomatal conductance and transpiration rate; 6. improving plant photosynthesis; 7. reducing the negative effects of drought on the host plant cell wall; and 8. reducing plant growth.
the arbuscule is a key structure in the AM symbiosis and that it is a dynamic structure that changes in size, number and morphology in response to the environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of the mechanisms by which the arbuscular symbiosis confers drought tolerance to host plants.
the molecular basis of AM symbiosis and how this symbiosis affects the response of plants to osmotic stress.
the study of molecular and cellular responses to water deficit in mycorrhizas and the identification of the genes involved in these mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AM symbiosis may improve plant water status and drought tolerance by increasing water uptake and reducing water losses.
AM symbiosis may be considered as a strategy to cope with drought stress, but it should be considered as a complex phenomenon involving several physiological and molecular processes.

the AM symbiosis confers drought tolerance to host plants through the combined effects of the increased uptake of water and nutrients, the improved root hydraulic conductivity, the reduced transpiration, the improved photosynthetic performance and the enhanced antioxidant system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AM symbiosis can alleviate the detrimental effects of drought stress on plants through the regulation of several molecular processes.
, in order to understand how the AM symbiosis alleviates the negative effects of water deficit, it is necessary to investigate the molecular basis of both the host plant and the AM fungus.
the AM symbiosis is a very important strategy for plants to cope with the stress of drought.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the AM symbiosis is able to modulate plant responses to drought stress, and this is achieved through the modulation of the expression of genes involved in the control of plant development and in the regulation of plant water status.
molecular studies of the AM symbiosis under water deficit conditions are needed in order to gain an integrated knowledge on how this symbiosis affects host plants under water deficit.
AM symbiosis can be a valuable tool to increase plant water use efficiency and drought tolerance in agricultural systems.
